// Code generated by go-bindings-codegen. DO NOT EDIT.

//go:build darwin

// Package shim lets a plain Go value act as an Objective-C delegate. The
// generated framework packages build one Objective-C class per delegate
// protocol (Class), create instances that remember which Go value they stand
// in for (New), and route each delegate callback back to that value (Value).
//
// The Objective-C side never stores a Go pointer: an instance is keyed by its
// own object pointer in a Go-side registry. respondsToSelector: is overridden
// per instance so a framework only sees — and only calls — the optional
// methods the Go value actually implements, preserving the behavior switches
// Objective-C frameworks derive from a delegate's method set. When the
// framework releases the last reference to a shim instance its dealloc
// override drops the registry entry, so the Go value becomes collectable
// again.
package shim

import (
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"unsafe"

	ebipurego "github.com/ebitengine/purego"
	"github.com/ebitengine/purego/objc"
)

var (
	selAlloc              = objc.RegisterName("alloc")
	selInit               = objc.RegisterName("init")
	selDealloc            = objc.RegisterName("dealloc")
	selRespondsToSelector = objc.RegisterName("respondsToSelector:")
)

// instance is the Go-side state behind one live shim object.
type instance struct {
	value    any
	responds map[objc.SEL]bool
}

var (
	mu        sync.RWMutex
	instances = map[objc.ID]*instance{}

	classMu sync.Mutex
	classes = map[string]objc.Class{}
)

// Class returns the Objective-C class named className implementing methods,
// building and registering it on first use. The class subclasses NSObject,
// declares conformance to protocolName when the Objective-C runtime knows the
// protocol, and adds two overrides of its own: respondsToSelector: (answered
// from the per-instance method set) and dealloc (drops the instance's registry
// entry, then calls super). It panics when registration fails — the generated
// callers pass unique, valid names, so a failure is a programming error.
func Class(className, protocolName string, methods []objc.MethodDef) objc.Class {
	classMu.Lock()
	defer classMu.Unlock()
	if class, ok := classes[className]; ok {
		return class
	}

	// The protocol object exists only after its framework is loaded; the
	// generated packages dlopen their framework before building a shim, so it
	// is normally present. Without it the class still works — frameworks that
	// probe with respondsToSelector: get the per-instance answer either way.
	var protocols []*objc.Protocol
	if proto := objc.GetProtocol(protocolName); proto != nil {
		protocols = append(protocols, proto)
	}

	all := make([]objc.MethodDef, 0, len(methods)+2)
	all = append(all, methods...)
	all = append(all, objc.MethodDef{
		Cmd: selRespondsToSelector,
		Fn: func(self objc.ID, _ objc.SEL, sel objc.SEL) bool {
			mu.RLock()
			entry := instances[self]
			mu.RUnlock()
			if entry != nil {
				if implemented, tracked := entry.responds[sel]; tracked {
					return implemented
				}
			}
			return objc.SendSuper[bool](self, selRespondsToSelector, sel)
		},
	})
	all = append(all, objc.MethodDef{
		Cmd: selDealloc,
		Fn: func(self objc.ID, _ objc.SEL) {
			mu.Lock()
			delete(instances, self)
			mu.Unlock()
			self.SendSuper(selDealloc)
		},
	})

	class, err := objc.RegisterClass(className, objc.GetClass("NSObject"), protocols, nil, all)
	if err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("shim: registering class %s: %v", className, err))
	}
	classes[className] = class
	return class
}

// New creates an instance of a shim class standing in for value. responds
// records, per optional selector, whether value implements the corresponding
// Go method; selectors absent from the map fall through to NSObject's answer
// (so the class's required methods always respond). The returned object is
// owned by the caller (+1); handing it to a retaining holder such as
// Associate balances that reference.
func New(class objc.Class, value any, responds map[objc.SEL]bool) objc.ID {
	id := objc.ID(class).Send(selAlloc).Send(selInit)
	mu.Lock()
	instances[id] = &instance{value: value, responds: responds}
	mu.Unlock()
	return id
}

// Value returns the Go value a shim instance stands in for, or nil for an
// object this package did not create (or one already deallocated). Generated
// delegate callbacks type-assert the result to the interface they need; a
// failed assertion makes the callback a no-op, which is the correct behavior
// for an optional method the value does not implement.
func Value(self objc.ID) any {
	mu.RLock()
	defer mu.RUnlock()
	if entry := instances[self]; entry != nil {
		return entry.value
	}
	return nil
}

// ── Associated-object lifetime ───────────────────────────────────────────────

// objcAssociationRetain is objc_setAssociatedObject's OBJC_ASSOCIATION_RETAIN
// policy: the owner retains the associated value until the owner deallocates
// or the association is replaced.
const objcAssociationRetain = 0x0301

var (
	associateOnce           sync.Once
	objcSetAssociatedObject func(objc.ID, unsafe.Pointer, objc.ID, uintptr)
)

// Associate ties value's lifetime to owner: the owner retains it (releasing
// any value previously associated under the same key) until the owner itself
// deallocates. key must be stable and unique per association slot — the
// generated packages pass the setter's selector (a SEL is a unique,
// process-lifetime pointer per selector name). This is how a delegate shim
// outlives the setter call even though Objective-C delegate properties are
// weak: the owner holds the only strong reference, and replacing the delegate
// releases the previous shim.
func Associate(owner objc.ID, key uintptr, value objc.ID) {
	associateOnce.Do(func() {
		h, err := ebipurego.Dlopen("/usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib", ebipurego.RTLD_GLOBAL|ebipurego.RTLD_LAZY)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		ebipurego.RegisterLibFunc(&objcSetAssociatedObject, h, "objc_setAssociatedObject")
	})
	if objcSetAssociatedObject == nil {
		return
	}
	//nolint:govet // a SEL is not a Go pointer; the runtime treats the key as opaque.
	objcSetAssociatedObject(owner, unsafe.Pointer(key), value, objcAssociationRetain)
}
